test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Rajesh, in his printing press, got an order to print some books, out of which he completed (17)/(27) of the order in 34 days. In how many days did he complete the entire order of printing?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In the fraction 17/27, the denominator represents the total work and the numerator represents the completed work.

17 units of work take = 34 days

1 unit of work takes = 34 ÷ 17 = 2 days

Total work (27 units) takes = 27 × 2 = 54 days

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction of the order completed = 17/27

Time taken to complete this fraction of the order = 34 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bf21276ede7d97d70373e49014b63c996e17c440423f07cc31ab41666943fca.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = Time taken for partial work ÷ Fraction of work completed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of days required to complete the entire order be x days.

⇒ Complete order is considered as 1 whole unit of work.

⇒ As per the given data, 17/27 of the work is completed in 34 days.

⇒ (17/27) × x = 34

⇒ x = 34 × (27/17)

⇒ x = 2 × 27

⇒ x = 54 days

**∴ The correct answer is 54 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method

It involves finding the value of a single unit and then multiplying that unit value by the required number of units to find the total value.

Work and Time Relationship

Work done is directly proportional to the time taken (assuming constant efficiency). If a fraction of work W is completed in T days, the entire work is completed in T ÷ W days.

Fraction to Whole Conversion

The denominator of a fraction generally represents the total parts, and the numerator represents the considered parts. Equating these parts directly to the given values leads to much faster calculations.
